metadata.note: Verbatim DDInter 2.0 slice for issue #195 - a presentation filed as a separate substance from its parent moiety, together with the sibling pairs that must NOT be merged with it. Rows are field-for-field their shipped-KB rows in KB order; the KB carries no interaction row among any of them, which is why 'interactions' is empty. Insulin lispro (protamine) publishes its own rxnorm_name and NO ATC code, so issue #192's correct resolution lands on it, the class comparisons have nothing to compare and the chip vanishes rather than being mislabelled; its parent moiety Insulin lispro carries A10AB/A10AC/A10AD. Dextran is the same shape reached through an ALIAS rather than a display name - the bare name 'dextran' is one of Dextran (high molecular weight)'s CIEL names and no row's display name. The iron rows are a third shape: Iron and Iron (bisglycinate) are already ONE substance (one rxnorm_name, one drugbank_id) while Iron (polysaccharide) is not, and none of the three carries an ATC code, so only the identity arm can reach them at all. Manganese (chloride)/(sulfate) and the two Varicella Zoster Vaccine rows are the negative controls: each pair shares a display stem and publishes two substance names, and the KB names no bare 'manganese' and no bare 'varicella zoster vaccine' anywhere - so a widening gated on the KB being NAMED the stem must leave both pairs apart. Peanut/Peanut oil is the residual shape that gate does not reach: two drugbank substances whose display names differ by a bare word rather than by a trailing qualifier.
